description_good_justification: README.md at https://github.com/dcondrey/guillochestudio/blob/main/README.md opens with a succinct one-line description: 'Mathematical guilloché pattern generation — engraving-grade ornamental geometry in the browser, exported as signed SVG, EPS, and PNG,' followed by an Architecture section.
interact_justification: README.md documents install/build (Quickstart section) but there is no documented feedback or contribution channel. The repo itself is private (confirmed via `gh repo view dcondrey/guillochestudio --json isPrivate` -> true), so no public mechanism to interact with the project exists.
contribution_justification: No CONTRIBUTING.md or contribution section exists in the repo root or README.md (verified with `ls -la` and `find . -iname CONTRIBUTING*`, no matches). No documented PR process for external contributors.
contribution_requirements_justification: No contribution documentation exists at all (see `contribution` above), so no acceptance requirements (coding standards, review process) are documented either.
floss_license_justification: No LICENSE file exists at the repo root (verified with `ls -la /Volumes/A/guilloche`, only README.md, CLAUDE.md, DEPLOYMENT.md etc. present). package.json has no "license" field and sets "private": true. GitHub confirms via `gh repo view` that `licenseInfo` is null.
floss_license_osi_justification: No license is declared at all (see `floss_license`), so it cannot be an OSI-approved license.
license_location_justification: No LICENSE/LICENSE.md/COPYING file at the repository root or in any standard location; only the Rust sub-crate packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign declares "license = \"MIT\"" in its Cargo.toml, but this is not posted as a project-level license file.
documentation_basics_justification: README.md provides Quickstart, Architecture (with a mermaid diagram), Workspace table, Engine API surface, Signed exports, Commands table, and Deployment sections — basic usage and build documentation for the software.
documentation_interface_justification: No reference documentation for external interfaces (e.g. the sign-worker's HTTP API in apps/workers/sign, or the AI worker endpoint) was found. README.md documents the workspace and commands but not request/response formats for the Cloudflare Worker endpoints.
sites_https_justification: Project homepage is https://guillochestudio.com (linked in README.md) and the repository is hosted at https://github.com/dcondrey/guillochestudio, both served over HTTPS/TLS.
discussion_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled on the repo (`gh repo view` shows hasIssuesEnabled: true) but `gh repo view` also confirms `isPrivate: true`, meaning the issue tracker is not publicly readable or open to new participants, failing the URL-addressable/public-searchable requirement.
english_justification: README.md and all other repo documentation (DEPLOYMENT.md, CLAUDE.md, FEATURE_ROADMAP.md) are written in English.
maintained_justification: `git log --since="90 days ago" --oneline` returns 43 of the repo's 50 total commits, with the most recent commit (808b495) dated 2026-08-08, well within the last 12 months and showing active, ongoing development.
repo_public_justification: `gh repo view dcondrey/guillochestudio --json isPrivate` returns `"isPrivate": true`. The repository at https://github.com/dcondrey/guillochestudio is not publicly readable, which is a hard blocker for badge criteria that depend on public visibility (discussion, report_archive, contribution, etc.).
repo_track_justification: Repo uses git; `git log` shows full author, timestamp, and message metadata for every commit (e.g. `git log --format='%an <%ae> %ad'` resolves author David Condrey <davidcondrey@me.com> and dates for all 50 commits).
repo_interim_justification: `git log --oneline` shows 50 granular interim commits (e.g. 808b495, 8bef171, ec3035f) representing incremental fixes and features, not just squashed release snapshots.
repo_distributed_justification: Repository uses git, a distributed version control system (confirmed by `.git/` directory and `git remote -v` showing origin git@github.com:dcondrey/guillochestudio.git).
version_unique_justification: package.json declares a static "version": "1.0.0" and `gh api repos/dcondrey/guillochestudio/releases` returns an empty array — no discrete versioned releases have ever been published, so there is no evidence of unique version identifiers being issued per release.
version_semver_justification: package.json uses "version": "1.0.0", which is valid SemVer format, and the release.yml workflow validates/derives tags in `v*.*.*` (SemVer) form.
version_tags_justification: `git tag` returns only "backup-pre-rewrite-tag" (not a release version tag), and `gh api repos/dcondrey/guillochestudio/tags` returns an empty array. No `v*.*.*` release tags exist despite .github/workflows/release.yml being configured to trigger on them.
release_notes_justification: No discrete releases have been published (`gh api repos/dcondrey/guillochestudio/releases` returns []); the project ships via continuous deployment (.github/workflows/deploy.yml deploys on push to main/staging via Cloudflare Pages) rather than discrete versioned releases meant for external reuse.
release_notes_vulns_justification: N/A because no release notes exist (see `release_notes`) and no publicly known vulnerabilities have been recorded against this project.
report_process_justification: GitHub Issues is enabled (`gh repo view` hasIssuesEnabled: true) but the repository is private (isPrivate: true), so there is no process by which the public can submit bug reports.
report_tracker_justification: An issue tracker exists technically (GitHub Issues) but is not usable by outside users since the repo is private, so it does not function as a public issue tracker for the project.
report_responses_justification: No externally-submitted bug reports are possible given the repo is private, so there is no majority-response track record to evaluate; criterion cannot be satisfied without a public report process (see `report_process`).
enhancement_responses_justification: Same root cause as `report_responses`: the private repository (isPrivate: true) precludes public enhancement requests, so no response record exists.
report_archive_justification: Any issues filed against a private GitHub repo are not publicly available or searchable by non-collaborators, so no publicly accessible archive of reports/responses exists.
vulnerability_report_process_justificati: No SECURITY.md exists in the repo (verified with `find . -iname SECURITY*`, no matches) and no vulnerability-reporting instructions appear in README.md.
vulnerability_report_private_justificati: No private vulnerability-reporting mechanism is documented or configured (no SECURITY.md, no security contact email found), so this criterion (which applies only if private reporting is supported) is not applicable.
vulnerability_report_response_justificat: No vulnerability reports have been received (no public reporting channel exists per `vulnerability_report_process`), so there is no response-time record to evaluate.
build_justification: An automated build system exists: package.json defines "build", "build:wasm", "build:packages", "build:web" scripts chaining Rust/wasm-pack compilation, workspace package builds, and the SvelteKit build, invoked via `pnpm build` and exercised in .github/workflows/pr.yml and deploy.yml.
build_common_tools_justification: Build uses pnpm (workspace package manager), Vite/SvelteKit, wasm-pack, and Cargo — all standard, widely-used FLOSS build tools for their respective ecosystems (confirmed in package.json scripts and packages/*/Cargo.toml).
build_floss_tools_justification: All build tooling observed (pnpm, Vite, SvelteKit, Rust/Cargo, wasm-pack, wrangler CLI) is FLOSS; no proprietary compiler or build tool is required.
test_justification: Vitest test suites exist across packages (20 *.test.ts/*.spec.ts files found under packages/guilloche-core/src/__tests__, packages/shared/src/__tests__, apps/web/src/tests, apps/workers/sign) plus supabase/tests/rls_policies.test.sql. README.md's Commands table documents `pnpm test` ("Vitest across every workspace package") as how to run it.
test_invocation_justification: Tests are invoked via `pnpm test`, the standard convention for a Node/pnpm project, as documented in README.md's Commands table and package.json's "test" script.
test_most_justification: apps/web/vitest.config.ts sets coverage thresholds (lines 70%, functions 70%, branches 60%, statements 70%) but there is no evidence in the repo of these thresholds being met project-wide or reported for guilloche-core/shared/workers packages, so 'most' functionality being covered is not verifiable from repo contents alone.
test_continuous_integration_justificatio: .github/workflows/pr.yml runs a `test` job (`pnpm test -- --coverage`) and a Rust `cargo test` job on every pull request; .github/workflows/e2e.yml runs end-to-end tests in CI as well.
test_policy_justification: No CONTRIBUTING.md or documented policy stating new major functionality must include tests was found in the repo.
tests_are_added_justification: Recent feature commits include test additions, e.g. commit 455e2c7 ("feat(studio): add settings panels for rosette, border and grid modes") modifies apps/web/src/tests/e2e/studio.spec.ts alongside the feature code, and commit e0904c5 ("test(e2e): make canvas comparisons stable and fail fast") shows active test maintenance.
tests_documented_added_justification: No contribution documentation exists (see `contribution`), so the testing policy is not documented anywhere for contributors even though it appears followed in practice.
warnings_justification: apps/web/eslint.config.js configures ESLint for the TypeScript/Svelte code, tsconfig.json and apps/web/tsconfig.json both set "strict": true, and .github/workflows/pr.yml runs `cargo clippy`-style "Run Rust lints" for the Rust/WASM crates.
warnings_fixed_justification: .github/workflows/pr.yml's `lint` job runs `pnpm lint` and posts a pass/fail status comment gating the PR (steps around line 87-159), and a separate job runs Rust lints (line ~348) with `cargo test` following — indicating warnings are enforced as part of the merge gate rather than ignored.
warnings_strict_justification: tsconfig.json and apps/web/tsconfig.json enable TypeScript "strict": true, and the CI lint job fails the PR check on ESLint errors (.github/workflows/pr.yml), representing a maximally strict practical configuration for this language/toolchain.
know_secure_design_justification: No document (SECURITY.md/README/CONTRIBUTING) states a developer secure-design rationale specific to this project, but this is a fact about the maintainer, not the repo — flagging unknown rather than asserting a false Unmet. Maintainer to confirm directly.
know_common_errors_justification: Same basis as know_secure_design: personal-knowledge attestation, not repo evidence — flagging unknown rather than a false Unmet. Maintainer to confirm directly.
crypto_published_justification: packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign/Cargo.toml depends on `coset` (COSE, RFC 8152/9052) and Ed25519 for COSE_Sign1 signing, and `sha2` for SHA-256 — all publicly published, standard, peer-reviewed protocols/algorithms.
crypto_call_justification: packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign/Cargo.toml uses established third-party crates (`coset`, `sha2`, `ciborium`, `zeroize`) for signing/hashing/CBOR rather than reimplementing cryptographic primitives from scratch.
crypto_floss_justification: All crypto dependencies (`coset`, `sha2`, `zeroize`, `ciborium`) are FLOSS Rust crates compiled via the open-source Rust/wasm-pack toolchain (packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign/Cargo.toml).
crypto_keylength_justification: Ed25519 (used for COSE_Sign1 signing per Cargo.toml) has a fixed 256-bit key providing ~128-bit security, which meets NIST-equivalent strength recommendations through 2030 and has no shorter-key configuration to disable.
crypto_working_justification: Observed algorithms are Ed25519 (signing) and SHA-256 via the `sha2` crate (hashing); no use of MD4, MD5, single-DES, RC4, or Dual_EC_DRBG was found in packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign/Cargo.toml or its usage.
crypto_weaknesses_justification: The C2PA signing path uses SHA-256 (`sha2` crate) rather than SHA-1, and Ed25519 rather than CBC-mode SSH ciphers; no known-weak algorithm was found in packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign/Cargo.toml.
crypto_pfs_justification: The project does not itself implement a key-agreement/transport protocol; TLS/PFS for HTTPS traffic is handled by Cloudflare Pages/Workers infrastructure, not project code, so this criterion does not apply to the project's own cryptographic functionality (COSE_Sign1 document signing, not a session-key-agreement protocol).
crypto_password_storage_justification: The project delegates user authentication and password storage to Supabase (an external managed auth provider, referenced throughout apps/web/src/lib/config/env.ts and the architecture diagram in README.md); the project itself does not implement password storage/hashing.
crypto_random_justification: Ed25519 signing (via the `coset`/Ed25519 path in packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign) uses deterministic signature generation per RFC 8032, and the signing key is provisioned as a Cloudflare Worker secret (apps/workers/sign/wrangler.toml, .dev.vars, gitignored) rather than generated ad hoc in application code; no custom/non-CSPRNG key or nonce generation was found in the crate's source.
delivery_mitm_justification: Software is delivered via HTTPS (Cloudflare Pages deployment, guillochestudio.com) and source is delivered via git+ssh (git@github.com:dcondrey/guillochestudio.git), both of which counter MITM attacks.
delivery_unsigned_justification: No hash-only integrity check retrieved over plain HTTP was found; all delivery mechanisms observed (HTTPS web deployment, git+ssh) provide transport-level integrity/authenticity.
vulnerabilities_fixed_60_days_justificat: No publicly known unpatched medium-or-higher severity vulnerabilities are recorded against this project; the repo is private with no public vulnerability disclosures found via `gh api` or search.
vulnerabilities_critical_fixed_justifica: No critical vulnerabilities have been publicly reported against this project to evaluate a response-time record against.
no_leaked_credentials_justification: `git ls-files | grep -i env` shows only apps/web/.env.example and apps/web/.env.test.example (templates) tracked; .gitignore excludes .env, .env.local, .env.*.local, and .dev.vars. A repo-wide grep for live-looking secret patterns (sk_live_ Stripe keys, AWS AKIA keys, PEM private key headers) found no matches; apparent hits (apps/web/scripts/validate-env.ts, apps/web/src/lib/config/env.ts, apps/web/.env.example) were confirmed to be Zod validation regexes/placeholder examples, not real secrets, and apps/workers/sign/.dev.vars is gitignored and not tracked by git.
static_analysis_justification: .github/workflows/codeql.yml runs GitHub CodeQL static analysis (javascript-typescript) on every push to main/staging, every PR to main, and weekly on a schedule.
static_analysis_common_vulnerabilities_j: .github/workflows/codeql.yml configures CodeQL with `queries: +security-extended,security-and-quality`, which includes rules for common vulnerability classes (injection, XSS, etc.).
static_analysis_fixed_justification: No evidence (e.g. a documented triage process, or commit history explicitly tied to CodeQL alerts) was found in the repo showing medium+ severity static-analysis findings are tracked and fixed in a timely way; CodeQL results are only visible in the private GitHub Security tab, not inspectable as repo evidence.
static_analysis_often_justification: .github/workflows/codeql.yml triggers on every push to main/staging and every pull request to main, in addition to a weekly Sunday-midnight cron schedule — satisfying 'every commit or at least daily.'
dynamic_analysis_justification: .github/workflows/e2e.yml runs Playwright end-to-end functional tests, but no dedicated dynamic security-analysis tool (fuzzer, sanitizer-based dynamic analysis) was found configured before releases.
dynamic_analysis_unsafe_justification: The project's memory-unsafe-language-risk surface is Rust/WASM (packages/guilloche-wasm, packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign), not C/C++; `grep -rn unsafe` across those crates' src/ directories returns 0 matches, i.e. no `unsafe` blocks are present, so this C/C++-focused criterion does not apply.
dynamic_analysis_enable_assertions_justi: No dynamic-analysis configuration enabling extra runtime assertions was found; packages/guilloche-c2pa-sign/Cargo.toml's release profile sets `panic = "abort"` and `opt-level = "z"`, optimized for size/production rather than assertion-heavy debugging/dynamic-analysis builds.
dynamic_analysis_fixed_justification: No dynamic security-analysis tool is currently applied (see `dynamic_analysis`), so there are no medium+ dynamic-analysis findings to evaluate for timely fixes.
